subject: MedPrime security discovery & air-gapped deployment scope
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-07T15:12:00Z
Subject: MedPrime security discovery & air-gapped deployment scope

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call highlights: 
- MedPrime is evaluating a private/VPC deployment of Redwood for clinical summarization and indexing.
- Primary concerns: HIPAA data flows, SOC 2 status (you indicated SOC 2 in progress), and whether an air-gapped/on-prem option is necessary for certain environments.
- Network: you mentioned segmented production networks with an MFT zone for PHI exchange and strict egress controls.

Immediate asks from our side: 
1) Please complete the attached vendor security questionnaire (vendor_security_questionnaire_MP.pdf) — helps us map where Redwood fits into your controls matrix.
2) If possible, attach a high-level network diagram (site-to-site VPN/VPC peering, DMZs, jump hosts) — a one-page PNG/PDF is ideal.
3) Clarify SOC 2 timeline and any specific control gaps you anticipate (log retention, processor agreements).

What Redwood will provide: 
- A short options doc outlining Private (VPC), Dedicated, and air-gapped on-prem setups and the tradeoffs (latency, key management, ops overhead).
- A proposed agenda for a 60-min technical deep-dive (network/firewall rules, subneting, KMS, egress allowances).

Proposed next steps & dates: 
- You complete questionnaire and send diagram by Tue 2027-04-13.
- We propose a tech deep-dive the week of 2027-04-19 — are mornings PDT better for your SecOps team?

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire_MP.pdf

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0162

Marissa — thanks for the summary and follow-up. Couple of items from our side: 

1) SOC 2: we are in the middle of our Type I to Type II transition. Expected Type II report completion: 2027-07 (Q3). We can annotate any interim compensating controls we have for production deployments.
2) HIPAA: PHI will be stored in isolated S3 buckets in our production AWS account; any third-party processor must sign a BAA.
3) Air-gap requirement: not required for our initial pilot but may be required for specific customer contracts (oncology partners) later. For now we want to evaluate a VPC deployment with strict egress rules and optional offline KMS.

Attached is a high-level network sketch we have (medprime_network_v1.png) — it shows the MFT zone, Prod VPC, and a proposed service subnet where third-party inference services could live. The diagram is rough but should help your architects.

We will try to complete the questionnaire by 2027-04-13; if we hit delays I will flag. For the tech deep-dive, Tue 2027-04-20 10:00 PDT works for our SecOps and infra leads.

Elena

Elena Torres
Senior Director, IT Security
MedPrime Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-08T12:30:00Z
Subject: Internal: MedPrime notes and proposed options

Marissa / Lauren — quick internal note after Elena's reply and the attached diagram. High-level technical bulleted plan we should bring to the deep-dive: 

- Option A: Private VPC (recommended for pilot)
  - Deploy Redwood Private control plane in our SaaS region, customer-managed Prod VPC peered via VPC peering or PrivateLink.
  - Use AWS IAM roles and S3 endpoint-only for artifacts.
  - KV cache and model weights kept in customer-controlled S3 (recommended).
  - KMS: customer-managed CMK for encryption-at-rest.

- Option B: Air-gapped/on-prem (scope if contractually required)
  - Requires shipped inference fleet + offline KMS/HSM for master keys.
  - No egress; model updates via physical transfer. Ops overhead and higher cost — call out that SOC 2 + BAA still necessary.

- Security controls to validate during deep-dive:
  - Required firewall ports and egress allowlist (we should send a minimal allowlist).
  - Audit log forwarding options (CloudWatch/CloudTrail or on-prem SIEM).
  - Retention policy expectations (logs, prompts) and deletion SLA.

Attachments: redwood_arch_options_draft.pdf (draft talking points for deep-dive).

I'll add a one-pager with minimal allowlist and a suggested agenda before we meet.

-Ben
